sources.name: BLM prescribed fire treatments
sources.coverage: Historical treatment units on BLM lands; Oregon-intersecting features from the OR/WA service.
sources.limitations: Treatment polygons are not observed burned footprints. Planning-document identifiers are often missing. Repeat treatments remain separate.

sources.name: USFS FACTS fire treatments
sources.coverage: Oregon hazardous-fuels fire treatment records on national forests.
sources.limitations: Includes planned treatments consumed by wildfire. Purpose codes are administrative; they do not fully explain site selection. Accomplished treatment acres do not measure fire footprint.

sources.name: PNW prescribed fire tracker
sources.coverage: Oregon-intersecting units in the regional planning and accomplishment tracker.
sources.limitations: Contains planned, in-progress, monitoring, and completed statuses. In Progress does not establish that ignition has occurred. Units can disappear without cancellation.

sources.name: ODF daily plans
sources.coverage: Rolling forest-management smoke records; public locations are points.
sources.limitations: Not all Oregon burning or all burn permits. A unit may have multiple ignitions. Empty responses do not establish no burning. Daily feeds enrich the three-day feeds and are not counted again.

sources.name: ODF daily accomplishments
sources.coverage: Rolling forest-management smoke records; public locations are points.
sources.limitations: Not all Oregon burning or all burn permits. A unit may have multiple ignitions. Empty responses do not establish no burning. Daily feeds enrich the three-day feeds and are not counted again.

sources.name: ODF three-day plans
sources.coverage: Rolling forest-management smoke records; public locations are points.
sources.limitations: Not all Oregon burning or all burn permits. A unit may have multiple ignitions. Empty responses do not establish no burning. Daily feeds enrich the three-day feeds and are not counted again.

sources.name: ODF three-day accomplishments
sources.coverage: Rolling forest-management smoke records; public locations are points.
sources.limitations: Not all Oregon burning or all burn permits. A unit may have multiple ignitions. Empty responses do not establish no burning. Daily feeds enrich the three-day feeds and are not counted again.

sources.name: Oregon Explorer recent wildfire perimeters
sources.limitations: Perimeter coverage is incomplete, especially for small and older fires. Perimeters and occurrence records are different views of fires, not additive counts.

sources.name: Oregon Explorer early wildfire perimeters
sources.limitations: Perimeter coverage is incomplete, especially for small and older fires. Perimeters and occurrence records are different views of fires, not additive counts.

sources.name: FPA FOD · seventh edition
sources.limitations: Occurrence points can be approximate. The catalog map-service link still serves edition six; this importer requires the seventh-edition SQLite download.

sources.name: WFIGS recent wildfire occurrences
sources.coverage: Year-to-date wildfire occurrence reports; retained snapshots preserve our observed history.
sources.limitations: Operational records are provisional, not a complete statewide count. Fire points are not perimeters. Historical years after FOD coverage require additional archives.

sources.name: ODF Smoke Data System history
sources.coverage: Historical registrations, authorizations and individual accomplishments to request.
sources.limitations: Export has not been received. No coverage inferred from annual totals.

sources.name: DEQ ecological burn permits
sources.coverage: Habitat and wetland restoration permit records.
sources.limitations: Permit approval is not evidence a burn occurred. Records not yet obtained.

sources.name: LRAPA / Rivers to Ridges
sources.coverage: Lane County ecological burn permits and unit map.
sources.limitations: Underlying GIS and historical accomplishments not yet imported.

sources.name: Agricultural field burns
sources.coverage: Willamette Valley field registrations, daily permits and accomplishments.
sources.limitations: Records not yet obtained; not a statewide agricultural-burning census.

sourceMetadata.description: HazFuelTrt_PL (Hazardous Fuel Treatments - Polygon) represents activities of hazardous fuel treatment reduction that are polygons. All accomplishments toward the unified hazardous fuels reduction target must meet the following definition: "Vegetative manipulation designed to create and maintain resilient and sustainable landscapes, including burning, mechanical treatments, and/or other methods that reduce the quantity or change the arrangement of living or dead fuel so that the intensity, severity, or effects of wildland fire are reduced within acceptable ecological parameters and consistent with land management plan objectives, or activities that maintain desired fuel conditions. These conditions should be measurable or predictable using fire behavior prediction models or fire effects models." The data came from the Forest Service's Natural Resource Manager (NRM) Forest Activity Tracking System (FACTS), which is the agency standard for managing information about activities related to fire/fuels, silviculture, and invasive species. FACTS is an activity tracking application for all levels of the Forest Service.

sourceMetadata.name: Recent Fire Perimeters (2000-2025)
sourceMetadata.description: The fire perimeters displayed in this dataset come from two different data sources published by the National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC). Wildfire perimeters through 2021 are from: National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC), InterAgencyFirePerimeterHistory All Years View. https://data-nifc.opendata.arcgis.com/datasets/nifc::interagencyfireperimeterhistory-all-years-view/aboutWildfire perimeters from 2022-2025 are from: National Interagency Fire Center. (2026). WFIGS Interagency Fire Perimeters [Feature Dataset] https://data-nifc.opendata.arcgis.com/datasets/nifc::wfigs-interagency-fire-perimeters/about . Accessed April 16th, 2026.The attributes of both datasets were simplified for use in Oregon Explorer tools by the Institute for Natural Resources at Oregon State University. QA/QC was performed to eliminate duplicate polygons based on incident names, however, some duplicate records may exist in the dataset because some fires had multiple incident names. See original datasets for full attributes (https://data-nifc.opendata.arcgis.com/datasets/nifc::wfigs-interagency-fire-perimeters/about and https://data-nifc.opendata.arcgis.com/datasets/nifc::interagencyfireperimeterhistory-all-years-view/about ).Important note: this is not a comprehensive dataset. Some smaller fires on private lands protected by the Oregon Department of Forestry, for example, are not included in these federally-compiled perimeter data sources. For ODF fire history please see: https://oregon-department-of-forestry-geo.hub.arcgis.com/datasets/geo::odf-fire/about
